title: Wallet Screening - Open App
meta_description: wallet screening for crypto address risk checks, AML context, sanctions exposure, and category-based review before transfers.
hero_h2: Check address risk before you move funds
hero_lead: wallet screening opens a focused crypto address risk workflow for reviewing chain context, exposure categories, sanctions signals, and audit notes before a transfer.
what_is: Wallet Screening is an app-first destination for reviewing crypto address risk signals before a transfer or compliance decision. The workflow is framed around transaction context, exposure categories, and documented review, aligned with FATF virtual asset guidance.

how.d: Enter the wallet address and confirm the chain so the review starts with the right transaction graph.
Check whether the address is tied to deposits, withdrawals, treasury activity, counterparties, or ongoing monitoring.
Prioritize category, hop distance, and sanctions relevance over a headline score.
Save the rationale, source links, and next step for an internal audit trail.

points.p: A useful result separates sanctions, mixer, fraud, exchange, and other exposure types so teams can respond proportionately.
Screening decisions should account for official list data such as the OFAC Sanctions List Service, especially for US-nexus activity.
Address formats and account models vary by network; Ethereum account basics are documented by ethereum.org.

faq.q: What is wallet screening used for?
faq.a: Wallet screening is used to review whether a crypto address has on-chain activity that may require compliance review, such as sanctions, fraud, mixer, or other high-risk exposure.

faq.q: Does wallet screening prove an address is illegal?
faq.a: No. A result is a risk signal, not a legal verdict; analysts should review category, distance, context, and documentation before taking action.

faq.q: Is wallet screening required for every user?
faq.a: Requirements depend on jurisdiction and business model, but regulated VASPs generally treat transaction monitoring as part of AML/CFT controls under guidance such as FATF virtual asset guidance.

faq.q: What should I check in a wallet screening result?
faq.a: Focus on the chain, transaction direction, exposure category, hop distance, flagged entities, and whether the result needs enhanced review or documentation.

faq.q: Can wallet screening create false positives?
faq.a: Yes. Shared exchange wallets, privacy tools, old clustering data, and indirect exposure can create noisy results, so human review remains important.
